label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Hey Hollins Family Ties — I wanted to say this before Thanksgiving instead of letting everybody wonder: yes, I’m coming, and I’m looking forward to seeing everybody. I want it to be a good day.

For the cousins who weren’t there last year, I got into a work/politics argument with one of my uncles at dinner, and it got ugly. I’m not interested in rehashing the whole thing or deciding a winner in the comments. He’s not a bad guy, he just likes to poke, and I clearly knew how to poke back. But that crack about him getting his news from a gas station TV was a cheap shot, and that part was me. I own it. He also sent me a thumbs-up for my birthday in August, which from him is basically a hug, and I appreciated it.

Grandma Pearl ending up out on the porch for about an hour is the part I still feel bad about. I’m not sorry for the work I do, and I don’t expect everybody to agree with it or with me. I am sorry for how I talked at Grandma’s holiday and for helping turn dinner into something she needed to get away from.

So can we call a truce on work and politics for Thanksgiving? Just one day. And to save us all some trouble: I really can’t talk about open cases because of confidentiality, so questions about “the lawsuit” are going to be a dead end, no matter how nicely they’re asked. Let’s keep the table to food, football, babies, and Tasha’s new boyfriend. That ought to give us plenty to talk about.

Thanksgiving is Thursday, Nov. 26, at Aunt Denise’s in Macon, and we’re eating around 3. I’m bringing mac and cheese and two sweet potato pies. Come hungry, and let’s have the kind of day Grandma can enjoy right there in the room with the rest of us.
